                    ### Question
                    A 3-day-old boy is brought to the physician by his mother because of irritability and feeding intolerance for 1 day. His temperature is 39.2°C (102.6°F). Physical examination shows a bulging anterior fontanelle. A photomicrograph of a Gram stain of the cerebrospinal fluid is shown. Further evaluation shows that the organism expresses the K1 capsular polysaccharide. Which of the following is the most likely causal pathogen?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Escherichia coli
opb. Listeria monocytogenes
opc. Pseudomonas aeruginosa
opd. Salmonella typhi
ope. Streptococcus agalactiae

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
A 3-day-old boy with irritability, feeding intolerance, fever (39.2°C), and bulging anterior fontanelle suggests possible meningitis. The Gram stain of cerebrospinal fluid revealing the presence of bacteria, along with the identification of K1 capsular polysaccharide, strongly indicates Escherichia coli as the causal pathogen. K1 polysaccharide is a known virulence factor associated with E. coli, particularly in neonatal meningitis cases. This aligns with consensus that E. coli is a common cause of bacterial meningitis in neonates, confirming it as the most likely pathogen in this scenario.
